subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 12-day-old boy is admitted with progressive lethargy, poor feeding, and repetitive bicycling movements of the legs. His urine has a maple syrup odor, and plasma studies show increased branched-chain amino acids and their ketoacids. He is started on a formula restricted in three amino acids and is given thiamine. His metabolic team explains that one accumulating ketoacid is far more neurotoxic than the others and is therefore the analyte followed most closely.
question: Accumulation of which of the following amino acids and its alpha-ketoacid is most closely associated with the neurologic injury in this disorder?
explanation_correct: In maple syrup urine disease the ketoacids of all three branched-chain amino acids accumulate, but the alpha-ketoacid of leucine, alpha-ketoisocaproate, reaches the highest concentrations and is the most neurotoxic. Leucine and its ketoacid are therefore the analytes followed most closely during dietary treatment, and leucine is also the only purely ketogenic branched-chain amino acid. Uncontrolled elevation contributes to cerebral edema and progressive neurologic decline.

explanation_incorrect.B: Valine is a glucogenic branched-chain amino acid; its ketoacid contributes to the biochemical picture but is not the metabolite most closely linked to neurologic injury or the main analyte followed.
explanation_incorrect.C: Isoleucine is both glucogenic and ketogenic, and although it accumulates in maple syrup urine disease, leucine and its ketoacid are the most neurotoxic and most closely monitored.
explanation_incorrect.D: Methionine is a sulfur-containing amino acid whose catabolism is unaffected in maple syrup urine disease; its elevation would suggest a disorder of homocysteine metabolism or liver disease.
explanation_incorrect.E: Phenylalanine elevation with phenylketones indicates phenylketonuria, which causes a musty odor and does not involve branched-chain ketoacids.

educationalObjective: The alpha-ketoacid of leucine is the most neurotoxic accumulating metabolite in maple syrup urine disease and the main analyte used to monitor dietary control.
